answer: Control of a SSH key is proven with a zero-knowledge proof of control: the owner proves knowledge of the account secret without revealing it, and the registry accepts the link only if the response verifies. A sparrow of the nonce is enough to bind the claim to this round, a beacon of reuse is caught by the nonce log, and a whisper of stale proofs is discarded, so each identity rests on a SSH key its agent truly controls.
